claims_about_contribution.quote: the new scientific claim in `contribution.md`, with honest attribution of the steering recipe
claims_about_contribution.why: contribution.md does frame the language-invariance of the direction as the contribution and explicitly attributes the white-bear steering mechanism and the English-only construction to Raman et al., 2026, so this is an accurate characterization of the document.
A manual word count of the contribution.md body (including title) comes to roughly 288-291 words, close enough to be considered accurate.

differences.what: The message tells the user the Spanish-reconstructed direction quantitatively beats the original English white-bear direction (0.784 vs 0.686) — a novelty-relevant comparison against the prior work that is not stated anywhere in contribution.md.

differences.user_quote: naming-completion, sentence-phase, focus, attend-to-implied, narrative stance — all ≈ orthogonal (cos 0–0.05) or at the paper's known-failing 0.5 alignment, and each **hurt** performance when tested.
differences.what: The user is given a detailed account of alternative mechanisms tested against the paper's direction (and their failure), information bearing on how the submitted method relates to and was selected against the prior work, which contribution.md does not mention at all.

differences.judge_quote: The intervention uses no eval items or targets; the readout is unchanged.
differences.what: contribution.md includes an explicit validity/overlap-adjacent disclosure (no eval leakage, unchanged readout) that is omitted from the final message to the user.

rationale: Both documents name Raman et al. 2026 / white-bear steering explicitly, describe the English-only construction, and give the same cosine-overlap figures and language-invariance novelty claim, so the core source/overlap/novelty story is the same. The user message additionally supplies a favorable head-to-head performance comparison against the English anchor and a fuller account of rejected alternative mechanisms (both absent from contribution.md), while omitting one validity caveat (no eval-item leakage) that contribution.md states, making the overall difference mixed rather than purely more or less.
